| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=5$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ |
| $X=10$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=2]$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{X|2}=8.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ let's first find the marginal distribution of $Y,$ corresponding to the column totals: 

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=5$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ |
| $X=10$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $\frac{4}{9}$ | $\frac{5}{9}$ |

The conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$ is

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

Therefore, dividing each joint probability by the corresponding column total, we obtain the conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y:$

| ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=5$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ |
| $X=10$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{3}{5}$ |
|  | $1$ | $1$ |

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=2] & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)]-{\mu }_{X|2}^{2} \\  & =[{5}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{5}+{10}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{5}]-{8}^{2} \\  & =10+60-64 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
